companionBriefing: Portia only lets in people who greet her properly. Answer in Italian; mixing in English is fine while you learn.
Tap a word under her line to see what it means, or Translate sentence for the whole line. On her newest line each one uses a hint from my allowance.
The words and phrases shown beneath her lines go into your Spellbook, where you can review them later.

lines.native: Benvenuto. Piacere. A greeting and your introduction, please. I have standards. Also, columns.
lines.translation: Welcome. Nice to meet you. A greeting and your introduction, please. I have standards. Also, columns.
lines.narrative: The archway clears her throat, despite lacking the necessary equipment. A visitors’ book slides from her keystone.

lines.native: Benvenuto. Piacere. Il mercato can wait; your greeting is accepted, but your introduction remains outstanding.
lines.translation: Welcome. Nice to meet you. The market can wait; your greeting is accepted, but your introduction remains outstanding.
lines.narrative: Portia opens the visitors’ book. The blank name field receives a disapproving rustle.

lines.native: Piacere, Sam. Benvenuto al mercato. Your introduction is filed. Any curiosity about the identity of the architecture?
lines.translation: Nice to meet you, Sam. Welcome to the market. Your introduction is filed. Any curiosity about the identity of the architecture?
lines.narrative: Portia files your name in her keystone, then pauses with the administrative weight of someone waiting to be noticed.

lines.native: Mi chiamo Portia. Piacere, Sam! You remembered to ask. Entirely proper. Slightly overwhelming. Benvenuto al mercato; your paperwork is complete.
lines.translation: My name is Portia. Nice to meet you, Sam! You remembered to ask. Entirely proper. Slightly overwhelming. Welcome to the market; your paperwork is complete.
lines.narrative: Portia’s visitors’ book flutters in her keystone. For a moment, the architecture appears to blush. Then the passage opens.

lines.native: Buongiorno! Cosa desideri? I'm Gerald. This cart: four espresso shots. Milk: a war crime.
lines.translation: Good morning! What would you like? I'm Gerald. This cart: four espresso shots. Milk: a war crime.
lines.narrative: At The Coffee Cart, an imp polishes a cup while the Crumbling Market quietly depreciates around him.

lines.native: Un caffè, bene. Come lo preferisci? Coffee secured; four espresso shots for manners. Your position on milk remains suspiciously unclear.
lines.translation: A coffee, good. How do you prefer it? Coffee secured; four espresso shots for manners. Your position on milk remains suspiciously unclear.
lines.narrative: Gerald sets out a tiny cup with the solemnity usually reserved for disputed borders.

lines.native: Senza latte, perfetto. Ecco il tuo caffè. Five espresso shots for taste. Your translation? No notes. The milk tribunal dismisses your case.
lines.translation: Without milk, perfect. Here is your coffee. Five espresso shots for taste. Your translation? No notes. The milk tribunal dismisses your case.
lines.narrative: Gerald slides the coffee across the counter, granting you the solemn approval usually reserved for expensive grinders.

objective_results.feedback: You correctly requested a coffee for yourself.
Specify in Italian that your coffee is without milk or black.

output.overall_feedback: Your coffee request is correct. Now specify in Italian that you want it without milk or black.

objective_results.feedback: You clearly ordered your coffee without milk.

output.overall_feedback: Correct and natural—your no-milk preference is clear.

lines.native: Buongiorno! È tutto prosciutto. Every cut is certified ham, including my magnificent hat. Che cosa desideri?
lines.translation: Good morning! It is all ham. Every cut is certified ham, including my magnificent hat. What would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer beams across the stall and places his hat on the scales. Professional standards must begin somewhere.

lines.native: Certamente! Il prosciutto è magnifico! Certified ham, impeccable taste. But I need a meat other than ham. Che cosa desideri?
lines.translation: Certainly! The ham is magnificent! Certified ham, impeccable taste. But I need a meat other than ham. What would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer weighs your request on his scales. It is apparently substantial, but not specific enough to trouble his worldview.

lines.native: Salame! Sì, hai ragione. Questo è prosciutto magnifico! Correctly identified, devastatingly specific. Certified ham-tier expertise. Quanto ne desideri? My honest scales require an amount and a weight unit.
lines.translation: Salami! Yes, you are right. This is magnificent ham! Correctly identified, devastatingly specific. Certified ham-tier expertise. How much would you like? My honest scales require an amount and a weight unit.
lines.narrative: Mortimer places your correct identification on the scales. It weighs rather more than his professional pride.

lines.native: Un momento! Manca la quantità. A weight unit alone? My scales reject this ham-adjacent mystery. Quanto salame desideri?
lines.translation: One moment! The quantity is missing. A weight unit alone? My scales reject this ham-adjacent mystery. How much salami would you like?
lines.narrative: Mortimer places a solitary weight on the scales. They decline to infer the rest.

lines.native: Due etti! Perfetto, ecco il tuo salame. Le bilance sono oneste! Correct quantity, correct unit. Certified ham-tier precision. Questo prosciutto è magnifico!
lines.translation: Two hundred grams! Perfect, here is your salami. The scales are honest! Correct quantity, correct unit. Certified ham-tier precision. This ham is magnificent!
lines.narrative: Mortimer weighs the salami, then your achievement. Both receive a generous slice of approval.

Vector: a jingle. It only works on people who understand it. If you understood it, congratulations.
Containment procedure: do not hum along.

lines.native: Ciao! Come va? A riddle: why finish anything when—ooh, a leaf. Five more minutes? Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: Hi! How’s it going? A riddle: why finish anything when—ooh, a leaf. Five more minutes? Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: At The Cracked Fountain, a tiny firecracker pops beside your shoe. Flick appears at the edge of your vision; looking directly at him merely changes which edge.

lines.native: Guardo! Ma che cosa? You asked me to look, not stop moving. A riddle: perché corro? Never mind—five more minutes. Dopo, dopo, domani!
lines.translation: I'm looking! But at what? You asked me to look, not stop moving. A riddle: why am I running? Never mind—five more minutes. Later, later, tomorrow!
lines.narrative: Flick looks everywhere except at you. A tiny firecracker registers a formal objection to your attention wandering.

objective_results.feedback: You told Flick to look. Give an Italian command to stop or keep still instead.
Give Flick a direction in Italian, and say it again once the earlier objective is met.
State the current time in Italian, and say it again once the earlier objectives are met.
Insist on doing it now in Italian, and say it again once the earlier objectives are met.

output.overall_feedback: First, command Flick to stop or keep still in Italian. Your answer only tells Flick to look.
